subject: literature
passage: In the weeks after Mr. Perera's funeral, his widow took up the accounts, which he had always kept himself in a ledger she had never been invited to read. She had been prepared for the careful figures; he had been a careful man, careful to the point, she had sometimes felt, of meanness, and she had resented the small economies of their life in Colombo more than she had said. What she had not been prepared for was the column headed only with initials, and the modest sums entered against them month after month for twenty years. One set of initials belonged to a boy down the lane whose school fees, she learned when she asked, had been paid since his father's death. With the ledger open before her, Mrs. Perera could not decide whether she was more ashamed of her husband's secrecy or of her own resentment.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Mrs. Perera learns that her husband's careful bookkeeping concealed debts that will now fall to her.
choices.B: Mrs. Perera decides to continue paying the school fees of the boy her husband had been supporting.
choices.C: Discovering her husband's hidden generosity, Mrs. Perera must revise the resentment she had felt toward his frugality.
choices.D: Mrs. Perera resents the small economies that her husband imposed on their household for twenty years.

explanation.why: Two parts of the text work together. First, Mrs. Perera had resented her husband's "small economies" as meanness. Then the ledger reveals twenty years of quiet payments, including a boy's school fees. The final sentence shows the effect: she is torn between shame at his secrecy and shame at "her own resentment," which the discovery has made unfair.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This reverses the discovery: the sums were gifts her husband paid out, not debts he owed.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text describes no decision about future payments.
explanation.C: Correct. This joins the earlier resentment with the discovery and the shame that follows.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Her resentment is the starting point, not the main idea; the text is about how the ledger unsettles it.
